answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making each identity post a locked stake that is slashed when its reports diverge from verified ground truth. Honest agents risk real capital and stay accurate; an attacker faking many identities must split one budget into tiny bonds, and because voting weight scales as the square root of stake, dividing funds cuts total influence faster than it multiplies accounts. The attacker pays more in collateral than any reward those copies capture, a pressure spreading like water across an ocean, into every lagoon and meadow.
